title: Emotions, moods and emotional intelligence
summary: What emotions and moods are, how moods affect performance, and the dimensions of emotional intelligence.

chunks.heading: Emotions and moods
chunks.explanation_md:
**Emotions** are an affective state of consciousness in which joy, sorrow, fear, hate, love, surprise and anger are expressed.

Common features of all emotions: they are **highly focused**; their **expression is universal**; and **culture determines the expression of feelings**.

The **6 major categories**: **anger, fear, joy, love, sadness, surprise**.

A **mood** is a feeling that is **unfocused** and **relatively mild in intensity**.

chunks.heading: Impact of moods on performance and the dimensions of EI
chunks.explanation_md:
**Moods affect performance more than emotions.** Moods strongly influence how much people help each other (**cooperation**), influence one's **attitude towards work**, and help **recall past events and actions**.

**Emotional intelligence (EI or EQ)** has four dimensions on the slide: **emotional attainment or self-awareness and people skills**, **emotional management**, **using emotions** and **self-motivation**.

questions.stem: Explain how moods influence behaviour and performance at work.
questions.model_answer_md:
**Moods affect performance more than emotions.** They strongly influence the extent to which people help each other (cooperation), strongly influence a person's attitude towards work, and help in recalling past events and actions.

Example: a positive mood can make colleagues more cooperative.

questions.stem: Explain emotions, the six major categories and emotional intelligence, and show how they matter in the workplace.
questions.model_answer_md:
**Emotions** are affective states of consciousness expressing joy, sorrow, fear, hate, love, surprise and anger. Common features: they are highly focused, their expression is universal and culture determines expression. The **six major categories** are anger, fear, joy, love, sadness and surprise.

A **mood** is an unfocused and relatively mild feeling. **Moods affect performance more than emotions**: they influence cooperation, attitude towards work and recall of past events and actions.

**Emotional intelligence (EI or EQ)** has dimensions on the slide: self-awareness and people skills, emotional management, using emotions and self-motivation.

**At work**: a manager with good emotional management and people skills can build cooperation, and awareness of moods helps explain changes in attitude towards work.

Conclusion: emotions, moods and EI together shape behaviour and performance.
